content: Master of the Revels at St John's, Clerkenwell
He reads with a pen, strikes little, and signs when he has been reassured. A wedding's cloth interests him more than a fifth act.
He licences what a yard may see, and he leaves the report to a man who was not in the room.
He can find a fault if he is asked for one, and this day he was not asked.
He will cut a lament he finds too long, and he will sign three books while saying nothing of the king.
